correction.text: the Burgundian Netherlands inherited in 1482: Flanders, Brabant, Hainaut, Namur, Luxembourg, Holland and Zeeland, without Artois, which the Treaty of Arras cedes to France in 1482

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Habsburg Netherlands row). The Burgundian Netherlands minus the Prince-Bishopric of Liège, as modern provinces. The infobox gives no area; later figures are on the Spanish Netherlands page (1560: 70,000 km2).

correction.text: the Netherlands with Artois, returned at Senlis on 23 May 1493

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Senlis returns Artois (but leaves Hesdin, Aire and Béthune with France). Franche-Comté and Charolais also return but are not drawn here.

correction.text: with Friesland, bought from Duke George of Saxony

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Lordship of Frisia ... after 1524'.

correction.text: with the Bishopric of Utrecht and Overijssel acquired in 1528

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'He acquired the lands of Overijssel and the Bishopric of Utrecht'; footnote 'Lordship of Overijssel (until 1528)'.

correction.text: with Groningen and the Ommelanden (1536) and, as the Union of Utrecht later shows, Drenthe

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Lordship of Groningen (including the Ommelanden) after ... 1536'. Drenthe is drawn because the Union page has it joining the rebels in April 1580; the Habsburg page gives no year for it (confidence 1).

correction.text: the Seventeen Provinces after Charles V re-acquired Guelders in 1543

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Seventeen Provinces after 1543 ... after Charles V had re-acquired the Duchy of Guelders'. The sum of the modern units is about 77,000 km2 against the Spanish Netherlands infobox's '1560: 70,000 km2' (ratio 1.1).

correction.text: 1579: the Netherlands without Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht, Groningen, Friesland, Guelders and the Union towns (Ghent, Ypres, Antwerp, Brussels, Breda)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Union of Utrecht signed on 23 January 1579 by Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht and Groningen; Ghent, Antwerp, Ypres, Breda, Brussels, three Guelders quarters and Friesland joined in the months after. The year-end shape; Overijssel is still loyal (it signs in April 1580).

correction.text: 1580-1584: the loyal south, without the Union's southern towns (Bruges and Lier joined in February 1580), with the city of Groningen, which Rennenberg returned to the king on 3 March 1580

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: matches the Union of Utrecht dossier's regions; the towns are radius readings. Revised after review: the city of Groningen is added: 'On 3 March 1580 he abandoned the cause of the rebels for the king' with the support of the city of Groningen (George van Lalaing page); Overijssel and Drenthe, which signed the Union in April 1580, stay out because the page says the rest of the province 'remained loyal to the rebel cause'.

correction.text: 1585-1587: the Spanish Netherlands after Parma's reconquest, with north Brabant (Breda included), the Meuse towns, Hulst and the city of Groningen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: about 53,000 km2 plus the Meuse towns against the infobox's '1600: 46,000 km2' (ratio 1.2). Breda was Dutch 1590-1624 (events). Antwerp fell in 1585. Revised after review: Groningen city (Spanish since 3 March 1580) is kept in the shape.

correction.text: 1588-1589: with the eastern towns the Dutch were to recapture in 1591-1597 (Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, Nijmegen, Steenwijk, Coevorden, Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, Oldenzaal)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review, confidence 1: the Eighty Years' War page lists the Dutch captures 'Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, and Nijmegen in 1591; Steenwijk and Coevorden in 1592; Geertruidenberg in 1593; Groningen in 1594; and Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, and Oldenzaal in 1597' but not when Spain took them; 1588 is the year of the Dutch Republic dossier's confidence-1 loss of 'the east' (page silent on when).

correction.text: 1590: Breda is Dutch

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'Maurice and William Louis subsequently captured Breda in 1590'; the first version kept Breda inside the north-Brabant province until 1628.

correction.text: 1591: without Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl and Nijmegen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, and Nijmegen in 1591'.

correction.text: 1592-1593: without Steenwijk and Coevorden

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'Steenwijk and Coevorden in 1592'.

correction.text: 1594-1596: without the city of Groningen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'Groningen in 1594'; the Rennenberg page: the city 'remained the scene of military action until 1594'.

correction.text: 1597-1605: without Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum and Oldenzaal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'and Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, and Oldenzaal in 1597'.

correction.text: 1606-1624: with Groenlo (Grol) and Oldenzaal, which Spinola's campaign brought back

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review, confidence 2: 'Spain recorded successes ... during Spinola's campaign of 1605-1606' (no place named); Oldenzaal and Groenlo are the two forts the Dutch Republic 'was able to conquer' in 1626 and 1627, so Spain held them again by then.

correction.text: 1625: Breda is Spanish again

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'the Spanish conquered Breda in 1625'.

correction.text: 1626: without Oldenzaal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'the eastern border forts of Oldenzaal (1626) and Groenlo (1627)'.

correction.text: 1627-1628: without Groenlo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: Groenlo (1627).

correction.text: 1629-1631: without 's-Hertogenbosch and north Brabant (conquered 1629), but with Breda, retaken by Spain in 1625

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Revised after review: Breda (Spanish from 1625 to 1637) is kept.

correction.text: 1632-1636: without the Meuse towns of Venlo, Roermond and Maastricht (Dutch, 1632); Breda still Spanish

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Venlo and Roermond were retaken by Spain in 1637 (the Dutch dossier cites a page for that); not drawn here. Revised after review: split at 1637 (Breda, Venlo and Roermond).

correction.text: 1637-1644: Breda is Dutch again; Venlo and Roermond (Upper Guelders) are Spanish again

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'In 1637 ... Breda ... was recaptured by the Dutch after a 3-month siege by the Prince of Orange'; the Cardinal-Infante gained 'the Dutch towns of Venlo and Roermond in the Meuse valley', which 'effectively cut Maastricht from the Dutch Republic'. Maastricht stays Dutch. The Spanish Guelders page: 'the capital Geldern with Upper Guelders remained in the hands of the Spanish' (confirmed by the Peace of Münster); Geldern itself is not drawn.

correction.text: 1645-1657: without Hulst in Zeelandic Flanders

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Peace of Münster (30 January 1648) leaves the south 'under Spanish Habsburg sovereignty'. Revised after review: Venlo and Roermond kept from 1637; split at 1658 (Dunkirk).

correction.text: 1658: without Dunkirk

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: Dunkirk, 'Spain's greatest base for privateers', surrendered to French forces on 24 June 1658, ten days after the Battle of the Dunes, and Mazarin 'handed the port over to the Commonwealth'. The first version had it Spanish until the Pyrenees (1659) and handed to the king of England.

correction.text: 1659-1667: without most of Artois, Montmédy and Dunkirk

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 7 November 1659, Pyrenees: France gains 'Artois and other towns in Flanders' and 'Montmédy and other parts of Luxembourg'; the English receive Dunkirk. Saint-Omer stays Spanish until 1677. Revised after review: Venlo and Roermond (Spanish again from 1637) are kept in the shape; Dunkirk left Spanish hands in June 1658 (previous keyframe), the 1659 treaty only confirms it.

correction.text: 1668-1676: Aix-la-Chapelle: France keeps Lille, Douai, Armentières, Bergues, Courtrai, Oudenaarde, Tournai, Veurne and Charleroi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'he kept Armentières, Bergues, Charleroi, Courtrai, Douai, Furnes, Lille, Oudenarde, and Tournai' (2 May 1668); Cambrai, Aire and Saint-Omer are returned to Spain. The Hainaut and Artois enclaves are radius readings. Revised after review: Venlo and Roermond kept.

correction.text: 1677: Valenciennes, Cambrai, Saint-Omer, Maubeuge, Aire and Cassel are lost to France

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1677 offensive 'intended to capture Valenciennes, Cambrai and Saint-Omer'; the Battle of Cassel meant the allies 'could not prevent the cities from falling into French hands'. Revised after review: Venlo and Roermond kept.

correction.text: 1678-1683: Nijmegen: France keeps Ypres; Spain recovers Charleroi, Ath and Ghent and (by 1683) Courtrai

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Spain recovered Charleroi' and Ghent was returned; Ypres stays French. Courtrai is a Spanish town in November 1683 (War of the Reunions page), so it is drawn as regained in 1678 at confidence 1. Tournai, Oudenaarde and Veurne are kept subtracted because no page opened returns them. Revised after review: Venlo and Roermond kept.

correction.text: 1684-1696: Luxembourg, Courtrai and Diksmuide taken by France in the War of the Reunions; Venlo and Roermond kept

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Courtrai surrendered 6 November 1683, Diksmuide on the 10th, Luxembourg on 3 June 1684; France kept them under the Truce of Ratisbon (15 August 1684). Revised after review: Venlo and Roermond kept.

correction.text: 1691: Mons taken by France

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: Mons, invested by Boufflers on 15 March, 'inevitably capitulated on 8 April' 1691 (Nine Years' War page); France evacuated it at Ryswick (Treaty of Ryswick page).

correction.text: 1692-1693: Mons and Namur in French hands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: Vauban invested Namur on 29 May 1692 and 'the citadel held out until 30 June'.

correction.text: 1694: Diksmuide taken by the Allies

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review, confidence 2: the Nine Years' War page has Luxembourg 'unable to prevent the Allies from capturing Dixmude' in the 1694 campaign (no date within the year).

correction.text: 1695-1696: Namur retaken by William III

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: 'Namur finally fell on 5 September' 1695, under William III.

correction.text: 1697-1712: Luxembourg, Mons and Courtrai restored by Ryswick; Ypres, Tournai, Oudenaarde and Veurne still French; Venlo and Roermond Spanish

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: the Treaty of Ryswick page names only 'Catalonia, Luxembourg, Mons and Kortrijk in the Spanish Netherlands' as evacuated by France; it does not name Ypres, Tournai, Oudenaarde, Veurne, Ath or Charleroi, so they stay out of the shape until 1713. The first version drew them restored in 1697, which the author called a bridging assumption.

correction.text: 1713-1795: the Austrian Netherlands: Belgium without Liège, Luxembourg, and the Roermond district of Upper Guelders

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after review: the Barrier fortresses of 1715 (Ypres, Tournai, Veurne) are Austrian, so the four towns are back by 1713 at confidence 1 (no page opened dates their return; the Treaty of Utrecht page names none). Upper Guelders was divided in 1713: Venlo and its surroundings 'became part of the Dutch Republic', most of the rest (Geldern) went to Prussia, and 'the land around Roermond ... remained under Habsburg rule'; Roermond stays here to 1795. Old note: no area figure for the Austrian period on the pages.

ledger.note: 1482: the Burgundian Netherlands pass to the Habsburgs. 'Upon the death of Mary of Burgundy in 1482, her substantial possessions including the Burgundian Netherlands passed to her son'; infobox 'Inherited by House of Habsburg: 1482'.

region.text: the Burgundian Netherlands, as modern provinces

ledger.note: 23 May 1493: the Treaty of Senlis returns Artois. 'signed at the French city of Senlis on 23 May 1493', the Counties of Burgundy, Artois and Charolais 'were returned to Habsburgs'; Hesdin, Aire and Béthune stay French. Under the 1482 Treaty of Arras Maximilian had ceded them 'as a dowry for the proposed marriage of their young daughter Margaret'.

region.text: the County of Artois, less Hesdin, Aire and Béthune

ledger.note: 1524: Friesland comes to Charles V. The infobox gives 'Lordship of Frisia and Lordship of Groningen (including the Ommelanden) after 1524 and 1536 respectively'; Charles 'purchased Friesland from Duke George of Saxony'.
1528: Utrecht and Overijssel. 'He acquired the lands of Overijssel and the Bishopric of Utrecht'; the infobox gives 'Lordship of Overijssel (until 1528)'.

region.text: the Bishopric of Utrecht and Overijssel

ledger.note: 1536: Groningen. 'Lordship of Groningen (including the Ommelanden) after ... 1536'. Drenthe is drawn with it at confidence 1: the Union page has Drenthe joining the rebels in April 1580, and the Habsburg page dates it nowhere.

region.text: the Lordship of Groningen with the Ommelanden, and Drenthe

ledger.note: 1543: Charles V re-acquires Guelders and the Seventeen Provinces are complete. 'Habsburg Netherlands (1482-1795) (Seventeen Provinces after 1543)' ... 'after the Habsburg emperor Charles V had re-acquired the Duchy of Guelders'.
1549: the Pragmatic Sanction makes the Seventeen Provinces one entity: 'the Emperor's Pragmatic Sanction of 1549, which established the Seventeen Provinces as an entity'.

1556: the Netherlands pass to Philip II of Spain. 'Following a series of abdications between 1555 and 1556' (Habsburg Netherlands page); Spanish Netherlands infobox 'Habsburg Spain gained Habsburg Netherlands: 1556'. Same state, Spanish branch.

April 1572: Holland and Zeeland rise. 'The period between the Capture of Brielle (1 April 1572) and the Pacification of Ghent (8 November 1576)'; the rebels 'seized several poorly defended towns and cities in Holland and Zeeland in April 1572'. The rebels are not yet the Union of Utrecht (1579); the slug is that of their later state. The States-General of all the provinces except Luxembourg joined the revolt with the Pacification of Ghent in 1576 and remained loyal to Philip II in form until 1581.

23 January 1579: Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht and Groningen sign the Union of Utrecht. 'The treaty was signed on 23 January by' Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht (but not all of Utrecht), and the province (not the city) of Groningen. The same month the Union of Arras (6 January) returns Artois, Hainaut and Douai to Spanish allegiance (Eighty Years' War page).

region.text: Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht and the province of Groningen

ledger.note: 23 January 1579: Holland and Zeeland sign the Union of Utrecht; the contest of 1572 ends as the loss below and the lands are the Union's.

Summer 1579: Ghent, Antwerp, Ypres, Breda, Brussels, Amersfoort, Friesland and Guelders join the Union. 'In the summer of 1579, Amersfoort ... also joined, together with' Ypres, Antwerp, Breda and Brussels; Ghent, Friesland cities and three Guelders quarters 'During the following months of 1579'. The month stands for 'summer'.

region.text: Friesland, Guelders, Ghent, Ypres, Antwerp, Breda, Brussels and Amersfoort

ledger.note: February 1580: Bruges and Lier join. 'In February 1580, Lier, Bruges and the surrounding area also signed the treaty'; the city of Groningen signs without a month.

region.text: Bruges, Lier and the city of Groningen

ledger.note: 3 March 1580: Rennenberg returns Groningen to the king. George van Lalaing, stadtholder 'in the service of Philip II of Spain from 1577 to 1581', 'abandoned the cause of the rebels for the king' on 3 March 1580 'with the support of the city of Groningen'. The page says the city 'remained the scene of military action until 1594' and that the rest of the province 'remained loyal to the rebel cause', so only the city is drawn; Overijssel and Drenthe (April 1580, Union of Utrecht page) stay with the Union. The Union page's February 1580 entry for the city of Groningen (above) is the event this reverses.
April 1580: Overijssel and Drenthe sign on. 'In April 1580, Overijssel and Drenthe signed on.'

1581: the Seven United Provinces secede. 'In 1581, in the midst of the Dutch Revolt, the Seven United Provinces seceded from the rest of this territory' (Act of Abjuration; the Union page: 'in 1581 the United Provinces declared their independence of the king').

1585: Parma retakes Flanders and Brabant. 'Parma's reconquests more or less stalled after the Fall of Antwerp (1585)'; the Union page: 'Flanders was almost entirely conquered by the Spanish troops, as was half of Brabant'. The towns are the Union's southern members; the page dates only Antwerp.

region.text: Ghent, Ypres, Antwerp, Brussels, Breda, Bruges and Lier

ledger.note: 1588 (bridging): the east is Spanish. The Eighty Years' War page gives the Dutch captures of 1591-1597 (Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, Nijmegen, Steenwijk, Coevorden, Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, Oldenzaal) but not when Spain took them; the dutch-republic dossier enters the same land as a 1588 loss at confidence 1 ('the page is silent on when'). Mirror of that event.

region.text: the eastern towns the Dutch recaptured in 1591-1597

ledger.note: 1590: the Dutch take Breda. 'Maurice and William Louis subsequently captured Breda in 1590.'
1591: the Dutch take Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl and Nijmegen: 'Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, and Nijmegen in 1591'. Mirror of the dutch-republic 1591 gain.
1592: the Dutch take Steenwijk and Coevorden: 'Steenwijk and Coevorden in 1592'. Mirror of the dutch-republic 1592 gain.
1594: the Dutch take Groningen: 'Groningen in 1594'; the George van Lalaing page: the city 'remained the scene of military action until 1594'. Mirror of the dutch-republic 1594 gain.
1597: the Dutch take Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum and Oldenzaal: 'and Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, and Oldenzaal in 1597'. Mirror of the dutch-republic 1597 gain.

1606 (confidence 2): Spinola's campaign brings back Groenlo and Oldenzaal. 'Spain recorded successes ... during Spinola's campaign of 1605-1606' (no place named); the two forts are those the Dutch conquered in 1626 and 1627, so Spain held them again. The dutch-republic dossier enters a larger 1606 loss in Overijssel and Gelderland drawn from Cliopatria cells; this event takes only the two forts the page names later.
1625: Spain retakes Breda. 'Spain retook Breda in 1625, and the Dutch recaptured it in 1637.'
1626: the Dutch conquer Oldenzaal: 'the eastern border forts of Oldenzaal (1626) and Groenlo (1627)'. Mirror of the dutch-republic 1626 gain.
1627: the Dutch conquer Groenlo: 'Oldenzaal (1626) and Groenlo (1627)'. Mirror of the dutch-republic 1627 gain.

1629: the Dutch take 's-Hertogenbosch. 'the major Brabantian city of 's-Hertogenbosch (1629)'; the Peace of Münster page lists 'cession of the Meierij' among the Dutch demands that were 'generally met' (1648). North Brabant is drawn lost from 1629 as a whole (Breda's 1637 recapture is the only dated further step).
1632: the Dutch take the Meuse towns. 'the fortified cities of Venlo, Roermond and Maastricht along the Meuse (1632)'.

May 1635: France invades the Spanish Netherlands. The Franco-Spanish War runs '19 May 1635 - 7 November 1659'; the French defeated the Spanish at Les Avins in May and besieged Leuven from 24 June ('on 4 July the French withdrew across the border').

region.text: Brabant at Leuven, and the Artois and Flanders border on which most of the war was fought

ledger.note: 1637: the Dutch retake Breda. 'In 1637 ... Breda ... was recaptured by the Dutch after a 3-month siege by the Prince of Orange' (Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand page); the Eighty Years' War page: 'the Spanish conquered Breda in 1625, but the Dutch took it back in 1637'. Mirror of the dutch-republic 1637 gain; Spain had held it since 1625 (previous gain).

1637: the Cardinal-Infante retakes Venlo and Roermond. The page gives the Cardinal-Infante's gains as 'the Dutch towns of Venlo and Roermond in the Meuse valley', which 'effectively cut Maastricht from the Dutch Republic', and no month; the year 1637 is that of the paragraph (confidence 2). Mirror of the dutch-republic 1637 loss. Upper Guelders stays Spanish thereafter (Spanish Guelders page: 'the capital Geldern with Upper Guelders remained in the hands of the Spanish') until the 1713 division. The first version drew Venlo and Roermond Dutch from 1632 to 1795.

region.text: Venlo and Roermond with their Meuse district

ledger.note: 1645: Hulst falls to the Dutch. 'Sas van Gent (1644) and Hulst (1645) in Zeelandic Flanders'.

24 June 1658: Dunkirk is lost after the Battle of the Dunes. 'Dunkirk surrendered to French forces ten days after the battle on 24 June' (the battle 'took place on 14 June 1658'), and Mazarin 'handed the port over to the Commonwealth'; Spain's garrison held it at the siege. The first version had the loss in 1659 to the Kingdom of England at the Pyrenees; in 1659 England was the Commonwealth/Protectorate (the commonwealth-of-england dossier records a June 1658 gain of Dunkirk, with France as its counterpart); the English sold it to France in 1662. The page gives no separate handover date.

7 November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees gives France Artois. France gained 'Artois and other towns in Flanders, including Arras, Béthune, Gravelines'; the Spanish Netherlands page: 'the French annexed most of Artois'.
7 November 1659: Montmédy and other parts of Luxembourg go to France ('Montmédy and other parts of Luxembourg').
November 1659: the Franco-Spanish War ends (infobox 7 November; the text says 'signed on 5 November 1659'); France keeps 'Artois and Hainaut along its border with the Spanish Netherlands'.

region.text: the Brabant, Artois and Flanders war zone

ledger.note: 24 May 1667: France invades in the War of Devolution. 'the French crossed the border on 24 May'; Charleroi falls in June, Tournai, Kortrijk and Oudenaarde 'by the end of July', Lille on 28 August.

region.text: Charleroi, Tournai, Courtrai, Oudenaarde and Lille

ledger.note: 2 May 1668: Aix-la-Chapelle. France 'kept Armentières, Bergues, Charleroi, Courtrai, Douai, Furnes, Lille, Oudenarde, and Tournai' and gave back Cambrai, Aire and Saint-Omer; 'further territory up to the current Franco-Belgian border was ceded' (Spanish Netherlands page).

region.text: Lille, Douai, Armentières, Bergues, Courtrai, Oudenaarde, Tournai, Veurne and Charleroi

ledger.note: 2 May 1668: the War of Devolution ends: 'signed by Spain and France on 2 May'.

1677: the French offensive on the Spanish Netherlands. The Franco-Dutch War ran '6 April 1672 - 17 September 1678'; Spain joined in 1673; the 1677 offensive was 'intended to capture Valenciennes, Cambrai and Saint-Omer'. The page gives no month.

region.text: Valenciennes, Cambrai, Saint-Omer, Cassel and Maubeuge

ledger.note: 1677: Valenciennes, Cambrai, Saint-Omer, Cassel and Maubeuge fall. 'the Allies were defeated in the Battle of Cassel. This meant that they could not prevent the cities from falling into French hands'; the Nijmegen terms give France 'Ypres, Maubeuge, Câteau-Cambrésis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel' (Aire is on the Treaties of Nijmegen page).

region.text: Valenciennes, Cambrai, Saint-Omer, Cassel, Maubeuge and Aire

ledger.note: 1678 (bridging): Courtrai is Spanish again. The War of the Reunions page has the Duke of Humières encircle Courtrai, a Spanish town, in November 1683, though France kept it in 1668; no page opened says when it came back (1678 is the Nijmegen year). Review follow-up: the Treaties of Nijmegen page was opened again and names neither Courtrai nor Oudenaarde (it lists Saint-Omer, Cassel, Aire, Ypres, Cambrai, Valenciennes and Maubeuge as France's gains), so the confidence stays 1.
Early March 1678: the French take Ghent and Ypres: 'captured Ypres and Ghent in early March'. Ghent is returned in September; Ypres stays French.
Early March 1678: Ypres is lost to France and kept at Nijmegen (the page lists Ypres among France's gains).
17 September 1678: France returns Ghent. 'France returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns in the Spanish Netherlands' (armistice 19 August, treaty 17 September).
17 September 1678: Spain recovers Charleroi and Ath. 'Spain recovered Charleroi from France'; the infobox: Spain regains 'Ath and Charleroi'.
17 September 1678: the Treaty of Nijmegen. Spain recovered Charleroi but 'ceded Franche-Comté, as well as much of Artois and Hainaut'.
November 1683: the War of the Reunions. 'Spain declared war on France on 26 October 1683'; Humières entered the Spanish Netherlands and encircled Courtrai on 3-4 November.

region.text: Courtrai, Diksmuide and the Duchy of Luxembourg

ledger.note: November 1683: Courtrai and Diksmuide surrender. 'After the town surrendered on 6 November, he then advanced on Diksmuide, which surrendered without a fight on 10th.'
3 June 1684: Luxembourg falls. 'Louis renewed the siege of Luxembourg in April 1684'; 'Its 2,500 defenders surrendered on 3 June'; France kept it under the Truce of Ratisbon.
15 August 1684: the Truce of Ratisbon: 'guaranteeing 20 years of peace between France and the Empire'; France retained 'Strasbourg and Luxembourg'.
8 April 1691: Mons falls. Boufflers 'invested the town on 15 March' and it 'inevitably capitulated on 8 April'. France evacuated it at Ryswick.
June 1692: Namur falls. Vauban 'invested the stronghold on 29 May 1692' and the citadel 'held out until 30 June'; the month is that of the citadel's surrender.

1694: the Allies capture Diksmuide. Luxembourg 'was unable to prevent the Allies from capturing Dixmude' in the 1694 campaign (no date within the year). France had held it since November 1683 (Reunions); the Ryswick page does not name Diksmuide, so it is drawn Spanish from 1694 and not as a 1697 restitution.
5 September 1695: Namur is retaken. 'In 1695, under William III, Namur finally fell on 5 September.'

1697: Ryswick restores Luxembourg, Mons and Courtrai. 'French forces also evacuated Catalonia, Luxembourg, Mons and Kortrijk in the Spanish Netherlands.' The page names no other Flemish or Hainaut town: Ypres, Tournai, Oudenaarde and Veurne stay French (the first version drew them restored, 'a bridging assumption'); Diksmuide is already Spanish since 1694 (Nine Years' War page); Ath and Charleroi (French captures of 1697 and 1693) are not drawn as lost. The treaty with Spain was signed on 20 September 1697 (the page does not tie the evacuations to a date).
1706: an Anglo-Dutch condominium. 'in 1706 the Habsburg Netherlands became an Anglo-Dutch condominium for the remainder of the conflict' (the War of the Spanish Succession).

region.text: the Spanish Netherlands under the Anglo-Dutch condominium

ledger.note: 1713 (bridging): Ypres, Tournai, Oudenaarde and Veurne are Austrian Netherlands. No page opened says when France gave them up: the Treaty of Utrecht and Austrian Netherlands pages name none of them; the Barrier Treaty page lists Ypres and Tournai among the fortresses of the 1709 plan and says the 1715 treaty 'reduced' the garrisons 'to seven, with a mixed garrison at Dendermond'. 1713 is the Utrecht year; the 1715 garrisons put them in the Austrian Netherlands by then.

1713: Venlo goes to the Dutch Republic. Spanish Guelders page: 'by the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713, Upper Guelders was further divided': Prussia took most of it including Geldern, the States (Dutch) Venlo and its surroundings, which 'became part of the Dutch Republic', Jülich the town of Erkelenz, and 'the land around Roermond ... remained under Habsburg rule'. The Dutch Republic dossier has Venlo and Echt (Generality Lands page); Echt is not drawn here and Geldern (Prussia) was never drawn.
7 March 1714: the condominium ends at Rastatt: 'the Southern Netherlands returned to the Austrian Habsburg monarchy' (infobox 'Treaty of Rastatt: 7 March 1714').

7 March 1714: the Spanish Netherlands become the Austrian Netherlands. 'The remaining Spanish Southern Netherlands became the Austrian Netherlands in 1714, after Austrian acquisition under the Treaty of Rastatt'; Lothar Dominik is the first governor (1714-1716).

1715: Dutch Barrier garrisons. The Barrier Treaty (1715) 'granted the United Provinces the right to garrison certain strongholds'; the page names no fortress (Namur, Tournai, Ypres, Menen and Dendermonde are the Dutch dossier's reading).

1744: France occupies the Austrian Netherlands. 'These were again occupied by France during the War of the Austrian Succession (1744-1748)'; 'again' refers to earlier French occupations. The page does not say which towns.
1748: Aix-la-Chapelle returns the land. The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle 'returned them to Maria Theresa in 1748'.

1781 (bridging): the Barrier ends. This page is silent; the Dutch Republic dossier of eu-09-j cites a page for 'In 1781, the treaty was declared void by Emperor Joseph II'. Review follow-up: the Barrier Treaty page was opened: 'In 1781, the treaty was declared void by Emperor Joseph II' and the treaties 'were cancelled by Austria in 1781'; it gives no date for the garrisons' withdrawal, so the end year stays confidence 1.
27 October 1789: the Brabant Revolution. The rebels 'decisively defeated the Austrians at the Battle of Turnhout on 27 October 1789'.
January 1790: the United Belgian States are established, 'established in January 1790' and without foreign recognition. Luxembourg stays Austrian.

region.text: the Austrian Netherlands, as the United Belgian States

ledger.note: December 1790: Austria crushes the revolution: 'the revolution was defeated by December' (after the Battle of Falmagne, 22 September 1790). The page gives no day.
December 1790: the Austrian reconquest ends the Belgian revolt.

26 June 1794: Fleurus opens the Low Countries to France. 'The Austrians gave up on contesting the Low Countries after the Battle of Fleurus (26 June)'; the infobox adds the Battle of Sprimont, 18 September 1794.

region.text: the Austrian Netherlands overrun by France

ledger.note: 1 October 1795: France annexes. 'On 1 October 1795 the departments were activated and the definitive annexation started'; Austria relinquished its claim at Campo Formio on 17 October 1797.
1 October 1795: the Austrian Netherlands become French departments (lead: 'Revolutionary France annexed the territory after the Battle of Sprimont in 1794 and the Peace of Basel in 1795').

region.text: the Austrian Netherlands, annexed as French departments

wars.name: Eighty Years' War (Southern Netherlands)

zones.text: Breda, the Meierij of 's-Hertogenbosch, Hulst and the Meuse towns
Holland and Zeeland, in revolt from April 1572
the north-eastern and eastern towns taken and retaken 1580-1627

wars.outcome: Parma retakes Flanders and Brabant (Antwerp 1585); the Republic wins Breda (1590, lost 1625, regained 1637), 's-Hertogenbosch (1629), the Meuse towns (1632) and Hulst (1645); Münster (30 January 1648) leaves the south 'under Spanish Habsburg sovereignty'.
wars.note: The page's infobox gives the war as 'c. 1566/1568 - 30 January 1648'; the war is entered from 1568, with the contest in Holland and Zeeland from 1 April 1572 (Brielle) and the Union of Utrecht in 1579 (earlier version: from 1579).

wars.name: Franco-Spanish War (1635-1659)
wars.outcome: Treaty of the Pyrenees, 7 November 1659: France gains most of Artois and Montmédy; the English receive Dunkirk.
wars.note: The text says the treaty was 'signed on 5 November 1659'; the table gives 7 November.

wars.name: War of Devolution
wars.outcome: Aix-la-Chapelle (2 May 1668): France keeps Lille, Douai, Armentières, Bergues, Courtrai, Oudenaarde, Tournai, Veurne and Charleroi; Franche-Comté and Cambrai, Aire, Saint-Omer are returned.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War
wars.outcome: Nijmegen (17 September 1678): France keeps Ypres, Maubeuge, Valenciennes, Cambrai, Saint-Omer, Cassel and the Franche-Comté; returns Charleroi and Ghent.

wars.name: War of the Reunions
wars.outcome: Truce of Ratisbon (15 August 1684): France keeps Luxembourg; Ryswick (1697) restores the reunions.

wars.name: Nine Years' War (Spanish Netherlands front)
wars.outcome: France takes Mons (8 April 1691) and Namur (June 1692); William III retakes Namur on 5 September 1695; the Allies take Diksmuide in the 1694 campaign; the Peace of Ryswick (1697) has France evacuate 'Luxembourg, Mons and Kortrijk in the Spanish Netherlands'.
wars.note: Zones added after review (Nine Years' War and Treaty of Ryswick pages).

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: An Anglo-Dutch condominium from 1706; Utrecht and Rastatt (7 March 1714) pass the Southern Netherlands to Austria.
wars.note: The war began earlier; the page dates only 1706 and the 1713/14 treaties.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession (Austrian Netherlands)
wars.outcome: France occupies the land; Aix-la-Chapelle returns it to Maria Theresa in 1748.

wars.name: Brabant Revolution
wars.outcome: The rebels win at Turnhout (27 October 1789) and form the United Belgian States (January 1790); Austria reconquers by December 1790.

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars (Austrian Netherlands)
wars.outcome: Fleurus (26 June 1794) and Sprimont (18 September 1794) end Austrian rule; annexation on 1 October 1795.

certainty.note: The pages give provinces and towns, not boundaries; the provincial frontiers are those of the Seventeen Provinces.
The frontier with the Union and the Republic moves with sieges; Münster (1648) fixes the northern one.
Treaty lines of 1659, 1668, 1678, 1697 and 1714 fix the French and Dutch frontiers; the Luxembourg and Barrier enclaves are approximate.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (13 pages opened for this dossier, over the nominal budget of 9 because the dossier spans 313 years and about 17 shape changes; the Nine Years' War page is the Palatinate dossier's). New state: Cliopatria has no Habsburg Netherlands row.

ONE STATE, THREE NAMES. Habsburg Netherlands (1482-1556), Spanish Netherlands (1556-1714) and Austrian Netherlands (1714-1795) are one state on the same land with two rename events (rule 2); the three Wikipedia articles are the sources. The Dutch Republic (eu-09-j) and Union of Utrecht dossiers already name 'habsburg-netherlands' as counterpart; the 1579-1590 and 1590-1645 events here are their mirror images.

SHAPES ARE MODERN-UNIT READINGS: Belgium minus Liège province, Luxembourg, Nord (French Flanders and Hainaut), the Artois region, Dutch provinces; circles for towns. Areas: 77,000 km2 (1543-1578) against 70,000 (1560, Spanish Netherlands infobox), 53,000 km2 plus the Meuse towns (1585-1628) against 46,000 (1600). Gazetteer names wanted (places, all drawn as lon/lat circles): Ypres (Ieper), Breda, Lier, Amersfoort, Menen, Dendermonde, Courtrai (Kortrijk), Oudenaarde, Tournai, Veurne, Charleroi, Ath, Douai, Armentières, Bergues, Valenciennes, Cambrai, Maubeuge, Saint-Omer, Aire-sur-la-Lys, Cassel, Montmédy, Dunkirk (Dunkerque), Diksmuide, Leuven, Maastricht, Venlo, Roermond, 's-Hertogenbosch, Hulst, Mechelen, Lille.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Franche-Comté (Free County of Burgundy), ceded at Arras in 1482, returned at Senlis in 1493, French in 1674-1678, was ruled by the same Habsburgs but is not drawn here; it needs a dossier of its own (the eu-09-g free-county-of-burgundy dossier ends in 1384). (2) The Prince-Bishopric of Liège, Stavelot-Malmedy and Cambrai (as ecclesiastical lands) are not part of the shape; Liège is its own dossier. (3) Tournai (1521 acquisition from France) and the 1501-1559 Habsburg expansion beyond what the infobox dates are not on the pages. (4) The pages do not trace Ypres, Tournai, Oudenaarde and Veurne after 1678; the 1697 event assumes they returned (confidence 2). The 1713 loss of Spanish Guelders (Venlo, Echt to the Republic, Geldern to Prussia) is in the Dutch dossier, not on a page opened here; the 1637 Spanish retaking of Venlo and Roermond likewise. (5) The Reunions page reports only the surrender of Luxembourg city (3 June 1684); the whole duchy is drawn lost (confidence 2). (6) Exact dates: the Union's June 1579 joins and the Treaty of Aix's 1668 towns use the pages' dates; the 1677 conquests have no month. (7) The Eighty Years' War page's own start date was not extracted.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: united-belgian-states (January-December 1790), franche-comte (Habsburg Franche-Comté 1493-1678), duchy-of-guelders, lordship-of-groningen, albertine-saxony (Duke George of Saxony, seller of Friesland in 1524).

REVISION 2026-10-25 (after review). (1) Ryswick: the 1697 gain is now Luxembourg, Mons and Kortrijk only (Treaty of Ryswick page: 'French forces also evacuated Catalonia, Luxembourg, Mons and Kortrijk'); Ypres, Tournai, Oudenaarde and Veurne stay French until a 1713 gain at confidence 1 (no page opened dates their return); Diksmuide is Spanish again from 1694 (Nine Years' War page, the Allies' capture in the 1694 campaign); Mons (8 April 1691) and Namur (June 1692 to 5 September 1695) are lost and regained as events, shapes and war zones. Ath and Charleroi (French captures of 1697 and 1693) are not entered: the pages do not say whether Ryswick returned them. (2) 1637: Breda lost to the Dutch (Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand page and Eighty Years' War page); Venlo and Roermond regained for Spain (Cardinal-Infante page, no month; year from the paragraph, confidence 2) and kept in every shape to 1713; the 1713 division of Upper Guelders (Spanish Guelders page) takes Venlo to the Dutch Republic (loss entered), Geldern to Prussia (never drawn) and leaves Roermond Austrian to 1795. The Cardinal-Infante page does not mention Upper Guelders. (3) North-east: the Rennenberg page dates the return of the city of Groningen to the king on 3 March 1580 (gain entered; the rest of the province, Overijssel and Drenthe stayed with the rebels on that page); the 1588 gain of the eastern towns is confidence 1 (no page says when Spain took them) and mirrors the dutch-republic dossier; the Dutch captures of 1591, 1592, 1594 and 1597 are entered as losses from the Eighty Years' War page; Spinola's 1606 campaign is entered as a gain of Groenlo and Oldenzaal only (confidence 2, since the page names no place and these are the two forts the Dutch took in 1626 and 1627). Drenthe and Overijssel as provinces are not drawn Spanish at any time: the pages opened name only towns. (4) 1568 and 1572: the Eighty Years' War page has 'c. 1566/1568' for the start; the war now begins in 1568 and a contest for Holland and Zeeland runs from April 1572 (Brielle, 1 April) to January 1579; the counterpart slug is that of the later Union of Utrecht. (5) Dunkirk: lost in June 1658 to commonwealth-of-england (Battle of the Dunes page: surrendered 24 June 1658; Mazarin 'handed the port over to the Commonwealth'); the commonwealth-of-england dossier names France as counterpart for its gain. (6) Nine Years' War zones: Mons and Namur. (7) Thin items: the Treaties of Nijmegen page (Courtrai) and the Barrier Treaty page (end of the garrisons) were opened and stay silent; both events keep confidence 1. (8) K8 and K9 now take Breda out of north Brabant 1590-1624 and 1637 on, as the events say. MIRRORS TO CHECK in the dutch-republic dossier (not touched): its 1588 loss and 1606 loss use Cliopatria-based regions while the events here use town circles; its 1713 gain is Venlo and Echt, here Venlo only. Gazetteer names wanted: Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, Steenwijk, Coevorden, Groenlo, Enschede, Ootmarsum, Oldenzaal, Mons.
